items.evidence: 26.1 worldgen/sculk.rs (727 lines) has no catalyst_chance/extra_rare_growths decode and no catalyst handling; decode reads only charge_count, amount_per_charge, spread_attempts, growth_rounds, spread_rounds; place() returns after the spreader rounds; the string 'catalyst' appears nowhere in the file. Vanilla 26.1 SculkPatchFeature.place (javap on the 26.1 server-game jar): after the spreader rounds, nextFloat() <= catalystChance with a collision-full block below places SCULK_CATALYST at the origin (flag 3), then extraRareGrowths.sample x origin.offset(nextInt(5)-2, 0, nextInt(5)-2) with air above and a face-sturdy block below places SCULK_SHRIEKER[can_summon=true] (flag 3); the catalyst roll happens BEFORE the growth sample, so the missing tail also shifts the RNG stream for features placed after a sculk_patch in the same chunk. 26.1 data: sculk_patch_deep_dark catalyst_chance 0.5, extra_rare_growths 0; sculk_patch_ancient_city 0.5, uniform 1..3. The 26.2 tree HAS the tail (sculk.rs lines 59-60, 97-112, 178, 188). items.evidence: The 1.21.7 world comparison measured water -1.04% underground with surface water matching; never root-caused. For 26.1 the mechanism is demonstrated, and it is total: the port never constructs a noise-based aquifer (see B6-G09). Pipeline::new reads the 26.3 'aquifers' config object from the noise settings; no 26.1 noise settings has that key, so the aquifer is None and generation uses DisabledAquifer - sea-level picker water only, no underground lakes, no flooded caves, no aquifer lava. The 1.21.7 deficit would be far larger in 26.1: ALL aquifer water is missing. The aquifer ENGINE itself matches the 26.1 jar (noise_based.rs byte-identical to the 26.2 file, spot-checked against the 26.1 jar: router-form ctor, 13 surface offsets, computeSurfaceLevel with OverworldBiomeBuilder.isDeepDarkRegion, FLOWING_UPDATE_SIMILARITY = 1-44/25); the defect is purely the wiring. Vanilla-side water: 4,876,455 blocks over 8,138 chunks.

items.evidence: Two sites in worldgen/sculk.rs require WATER_SOURCE where the 26.1 jar tests fluid-is-water: sculk.rs:305 (attempt_spread_vein, Default branch, non-empty facings) and sculk.rs:548 (can_place_growth above-open gate). Vanilla 26.1: SculkBehaviour$1.attemptSpreadVein regrows when the state is air OR fluidState.is(Fluids.WATER); SculkBlock.canPlaceGrowth accepts above air OR (is(WATER) AND fluidState.is(WATER)). The port's WATER_SOURCE is set only for source water (tree_blocks.rs:184; flowing water gets WATER_FLUID|ANY_FLUID only), so flowing water blocks sculk vein regrowth and growth placement that vanilla allows. items.evidence: Pipeline::new (generator.rs:1126-1129) reads settings_json["aquifers"] - a 26.3 config-object key - and builds the aquifer config from it. NO 26.1 noise settings has that key (all 7 checked: overworld, amplified and large_biomes have aquifers_enabled: true; caves, end, floating_islands, nether false; none has 'aquifers'). So the aquifer is always None and generation uses DisabledAquifer (generator.rs:1770, 2031): density <= 0 -> the global fluid picker only (sea-level water), no barrier/floodedness/spread noise, no underground lakes or flooded caves. Vanilla 26.1 builds NoiseBasedAquifer from the ROUTER (jar ctor takes the NoiseRouter and reads barrierNoise, fluidLevelFloodednessNoise, fluidLevelSpreadNoise, lavaNoise, erosion, depth). The 26.2 tree fixed exactly this (from_router + aquifers_enabled gate, generator.rs:1164-1171, with synthesize::aquifer_exclusion); the 26.1 tree has neither from_router nor any aquifer_exclusion synthesis. Silent: no error is raised, the aquifer is just absent. Mechanism behind B6-G03.
items.title: Aquifers entirely disabled: Pipeline::new reads the 26.3 'aquifers' config object, absent from all 26.1 settings

items.evidence: worldgen/router.rs declares 8 fields (temperature, vegetation, continents, erosion, depth, ridges, chunk_surface_level, final_density) and from_json requires all of them. The 26.1 jar's NoiseRouter record has 15 components (barrier, fluid_level_floodedness, fluid_level_spread, lava, preliminary_surface_level, vein_toggle, vein_ridged, vein_gap, plus the eight) - there is NO chunk_surface_level in 26.1. All 7 prepared noise settings lack that key, so NoiseRouter::from_json errors at generator.rs:1105 for every settings object, before the aquifer, rule and spawn-target steps. OverworldGenerator::for_world_with_settings (the real world-construction path) and the flat path both go through Pipeline::new, so no noise or flat world can be constructed. The 26.2 tree has the correct 15-field form (router.rs, ALL: [Self; 15], PreliminarySurfaceLevel). Second failure in the construction cascade (after G06).
items.title: NoiseRouter is the 26.3 eight-field form (requires chunk_surface_level); Pipeline::new fails on 26.1 settings

No 26.1 noise settings has a material_rule key - they carry an inline surface_rule object ({type: sequence, ...}), the 1.21.x/26.2 form, and rules.json/conditions.json are legitimately empty (no such data folders exist in the 26.1 jar; SurfaceRules are inline in the settings). items.evidence: generator.rs:1153-1175 decodes each spawn_target point by mapping every field name through library.named_density(name) - looking up a density function named minecraft:<field>. None of the 7 field names used by the 26.1 overworld/amplified/large_biomes spawn targets (continentalness, depth, erosion, humidity, offset, temperature, weirdness) is a registered density function (the 35 registry entries are all minecraft:overworld/..., minecraft:end/..., minecraft:nether/..., minecraft:shift_x, minecraft:shift_z, minecraft:y, minecraft:zero), so the decode errors with 'unknown material density' for every settings object with a non-empty spawn_target. Latent second half: even if the lookups resolved, SpawnTargetPoint::sample_fitness samples each named density, but vanilla's Climate$SpawnFinder.getSpawnPositionAndFitness rebuilds the sampled TargetPoint with depth FORCED to 0 (javap: lconst_0 as the depth argument) and adds square(offset) as a constant. The 26.1 overworld depth function at y=0 is ~1.0 + the offset spline (NOT 0), so sampling it would add a large position-varying bias to every candidate's fitness. The 26.2 tree decodes spawn_target via decode_parameter_point and its spawn_finder zeroes the depth. The radial-search/fitness FORMULA in the port matches the jar exactly; only the decode and the depth handling are wrong.
items.title: spawn_target decode fails (named-density lookups for bare climate field names); depth not zeroed

items.evidence: worldgen/density.rs has no arms for cache_2d, cache_once, flat_cache or shifted_noise; the default arm errors 'unknown density type: {kind}'. All four are used in 26.1 data: minecraft:overworld/offset is flat_cache > cache_2d > add(...) (with cache_once around blend_alpha inside) - and offset is an argument of minecraft:overworld/depth, a router field, so decoding the router's depth function fails; cache_2d x13 and shifted_noise x8 in the noise settings' surface rules; cache_2d x2 / flat_cache x2 across the density-function registry. The 26.2 tree has all four arms (density.rs:362 cache_2d|cache_once|flat_cache, :402 noise|shifted_noise); the 26.1 compiler even has a ShiftedNoiseSampler (horizon-core/src/density/mod.rs:437) that the JSON decoder never produces. Fires during the router decode in Pipeline::new (after G10's missing-field error, before G11).

items.evidence: Top-level configured-feature types in the 26.1 data: 53 distinct, 221 total. Eleven have NO arm in the port's feature dispatch (feature_graph.rs, plus feature.rs for the end features) - the default arm falls through to BasicFeature::from_json, which errors 'basic feature type' for anything but the three end features: basalt_columns x2, basalt_pillar x1, desert_well x1, dripstone_cluster x1, glowstone_blob x1, kelp x1, nether_forest_vegetation x6, sea_pickle x1, seagrass x4, twisting_vines x2, weeping_vines x1. All except dripstone_cluster have arms in the 26.2 tree (kelp/seagrass/sea_pickle via aquatic.rs, a file absent in 26.1; twisting/weeping vines via nether.rs); dripstone_cluster is missing in BOTH trees (both carry the 26.3 name speleothem_cluster instead). Plus coral_mushroom, nested inside warm_ocean_vegetation's simple_random_selector (dispatch has coral_tree|coral_claw only; CoralFeature::decode errors on other kinds). Feature decoding is lazy (FeatureCatalog::named), so these fail at decoration time when a chunk references one of the 24 placed features. Also missing: the nether_cave carver arm (carver/generation.rs has cave + canyon only; 26.2 has cave | nether_cave); the 5 nether biomes list minecraft:nether_cave as their carver.

source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 6 — checks + triage only, no fixes. Scope: noise/density functions, carvers, configured/placed features, structures and structure sets, template pools, biomes and biome sources, chunk generation stages, spawn finding, world presets. Static checks only (javap + source + data diffs + vanilla world census); no cargo builds, no driver runs, no commits.
systemic_note: Unlike 26.2, this batch HAS a single systemic cause across most of its open defects: the 26.1 tree still carries the 26.3 forms where 26.1 uses the 1.21.x forms — the prepare folder names (G06), the NoiseRouter (G10), the aquifer config object (G09), the material-rule name (G11), the spawn-target named densities (G12), the density cache/shifted-noise arms (G13), and 11 feature types + the nether carver (G14) were all fixed in the 26.2 tree and are all still 26.3-form in 26.1. The 26.2 tree is the repair template for every one of them. The sculk defects (G01/G05/G07/G08) are the exception: same narrow-predicate pattern as 26.2's G05, found only by javap-diffing the feature's gates. Arm presence is not correctness — G05, G07 and G08 were silent narrowings inside present arms, found only by javap-diffing. Three of the four 1.21.7 defects reproduce in 26.1 (G01, G03, G05); only G02 and G04 are withdrawn. The 26.1 port is materially less faithful on worldgen than the 26.2 tree was at sweep time: no 26.1 world can generate at all with the current tree + prepared data.
